anchor.surface_text: Though this contention might, at first thought, sound plausible, a closer examination of the language of section 17 shows that this is number its true import. The section does number enact that persons who are disqualified under a law made by Parliament shall be disqualified to be chosen under the Act. What it does enact is that if a person would be disqualified to be chosen to either House under an Act of Parliament, he would be dis- qualified to be chosen for the State Assembly.

holdings.text: Section 17 of Act No. XLIX of 1951 incorporates the disqualifications under Article 102(1)(e) of the Constitution such that a person disqualified for membership of Parliament under any law made by Parliament, including section 7(d) of Act No. XLIII of 1951, is also disqualified for membership of the Legislative Assembly in Part C States, irrespective of whether Act No. XLIII applies proprio vigore to such elections.
holdings.reasoning_summary: Textual analysis of Section 17 rejects the need for proprio vigore application of Act XLIII to Part C States; disqualification for Parliament via parliamentary law automatically applies to Part C assemblies; addresses harmonious construction argument preliminarily.
